asks: Is Nix the base of recipes?
answer: Silo builds each recipe with Nix, which pins every package to an exact version and checks its signature, so the same recipe makes the same computer again. A user does not write Nix: a recipe names packages and pieces, and Silo turns it into Nix, as devbox and Flox do. Whoever writes a new piece may use Nix inside it. What Nix cannot describe, Silo does as steps of its own. If Nix cannot build a recipe, no computer is made, and Silo shows the package that failed and why. To find out: what the first build of a recipe costs in time and disk.
